text.en:
Creation of the Presidential Task Force. - There is hereby
created a Presidential Task Force for MRB Rehabilitation and Development
(hereafter referred to as the "Task Force") for the proper and effective
implementation o government interventions for the disaster-affected
population in the Provinces of North Cotabato, South Cotabato, Sarangani and
Sultan Kudarat, and the cities of Cotabato and General Santos of Region XII,
and Maguindanao, Shariff Kabunsuan and Lanao del Sur of the ARMM,
otherwise known as "MRB affected areas"
The Task Force shall be composed of the following:
Chairperson
Co-Chairperson

Powers and Functions of the Task Force. - The Task Force
shall have the following powers and functions:
Coordinate the formulation and implementation of the MRB Relief,
Rehabilitation and Long Term Development Plan;
Negotiate, apply for, receive and accept grants and donation of
funds needed for the relief, rehabilitation and development of the
areas affected by the disaster;
Decide on important interventions that need to be immediately
implemented or acted upon;
Identify and package relief, rehabilitation and long term
interventions for the MRB affected areas;
Spearhead and coordinate all actions to rehabilitate and develop
the MRB affected areas;
Conduct resource mobilization activities, such as, but not limited
i. Enjoining the concerned LGUs to pass ordinances appropriating
local resources for identified interventions:
il. Requesting NDCC funds;
i. Ensuring inclusion of rehabilitation plans of Regional Line
Agencies in their annual operational plans or realign funds, if
iv. Conducting special Official Development Assistance (ODA)
pledging sessions to be spearheaded by the RDC/REDPB and
RDCCs of Region XII and ARMM;
v. Enjoining Congress to include a special purpose fund for
rehabilitation and development in the General Appropriations
Act for FY 2009 and beyond.
g. Perform other activities pursuant to the orders of the President.

Support Office. - The Task Force shall have a Support Office
that will provide day-to-day technical, administrative and financial services. It
shall be accountable for the funds, records and properties of the Task Force. It
shall be headed by a Director with the following staff composition, namely;
Development Management Officer, Project Management Officer, Project
Evaluation Officer, Administrative Officer, Accountant, Disbursing Officer,
Secretary, Clerk/Computer Operator, Driver and Utility Worker.

Technical Working Groups. - The Task Force shall be
assisted in the performance of its functions by the Technical Working Groups
(TWGs) on relief, rehabilitation and long-term development. They shall perform
functions supportive to the Task Force. They shall review and endorse
programs, projects, activities and other relevant matters pertaining to their
respective assignments.

Timeline. - The Task Force shall be in operation for two (2)
consecutive years from the issuance of this Executive Order, without prejudice
to the extension of time to be granted by the President as may be deemed
necessary to accomplish its tasks.

Budget Support. - The Task Force shall be allocated an
initial operating fund of Ten Million Pesos (P10 Million) to be sourced from the
President's Contingent Fund. Succeeding outlays shall be provided under the
General Appropriations Acts, as deemed necessary.

Submission of Periodic Reports to the President.
Task Force shall submit update reports to the Office of the President, through
the Presidential Management Staff, every six (6) months to inform the President
of the progress of work being done by the Task Force.

Agency Assistance. - All departments, bureaus, offices,
agencies or instrumentalities, including government-owned and /or -controlled
corporations, are hereby directed to extend such assistance and cooperation as
the Task Force may need in the discharge of its functions.

Repealing Clause. - All other orders, rules, regulations and
issuances, or parts thereof, which are inconsistent with this Executive Order
are hereby repealed or modified accordingly.
